strings.d1.s0.name: Westminster Abbey
strings.d1.s0.tips: The royal coronation church. Book tickets online (~30 GBP) and arrive at 09:30 to avoid a queue at the entrance.
strings.d1.s1.name: Big Ben & Houses of Parliament
strings.d1.s1.tips: Get the classic photo from Westminster Bridge. Parliament tours are booked separately.
strings.d1.s2.name: Borough Market
strings.d1.s2.tips: London's food market: try the Kappacasein raclette and a Bread Ahead doughnut, and eat lunch standing up.
strings.d1.s3.name: Tate Modern
strings.d1.s3.tips: Modern art in a former power station. Entry is free, and the 10th-floor viewing terrace has great views.
strings.d1.s4.name: South Bank Walk
strings.d1.s4.tips: Follow the Thames from the Millennium Bridge to the London Eye, past street performers and a book market.
strings.d1.b0.name: Padella Borough
strings.d1.b0.tips: Handmade pasta. Join the queue through the app.
strings.d1.b1.name: London Eye
strings.d1.b1.tips: The observation wheel. Book online and go at sunset.
strings.d2.s0.name: Tower of London
strings.d2.s0.tips: The Crown Jewels and a Beefeater tour. Enter at the 09:00 opening and head straight for the jewels. Online ~37 GBP.
strings.d2.s1.name: Tower Bridge
strings.d2.s1.tips: Walk across the bridge. The glass-floored walkway needs a separate ticket (~13 GBP).
strings.d2.s2.name: St Dunstan in the East
strings.d2.s2.tips: The garden ruins of a bombed church, a hidden corner of the city.
strings.d2.s3.name: Leadenhall Market
strings.d2.s3.tips: A Victorian market hall (seen in Harry Potter). Have a pub lunch here.
strings.d2.s4.name: St Paul's Cathedral
strings.d2.s4.tips: Wren's dome. Climb 528 steps to the Golden Gallery for the view.
strings.d2.b0.name: Sky Garden
strings.d2.b0.tips: The free garden terrace at the Walkie Talkie. Reserve online in advance.
strings.d2.b1.name: The Dickens Inn St Katharine Docks
strings.d2.b1.tips: A marina pub next to Tower Bridge. Order the fish and chips.
strings.d3.s0.name: British Museum
strings.d3.s0.tips: The Rosetta Stone and the Parthenon marbles. Free entry, opens at 10:00, and don't miss the Great Court.
strings.d3.s1.name: Dishoom Covent Garden
strings.d3.s1.tips: A Bombay-style café. Order the black daal and bacon naan; expect a 20-minute queue.
strings.d3.s2.name: Covent Garden
strings.d3.s2.tips: Street performances on the Piazza and the Apple Market.
strings.d3.s3.name: Soho & Carnaby Street
strings.d3.s3.tips: Boutiques and Chinatown, plus Berwick Street Market.
strings.d3.s4.name: The French House Soho
strings.d3.s4.tips: Soho's literary pub, with a tradition of serving half pints.
strings.d3.b0.name: National Gallery
strings.d3.b0.tips: Van Gogh and Turner on Trafalgar Square. Free entry; an alternative to the museum.
strings.d3.b1.name: Bao Soho
strings.d3.b1.tips: Taiwanese bao buns, quick and famous.
strings.d4.theme: Notting Hill, Kensington and Hyde Park
strings.d4.s0.name: Portobello Road Market
strings.d4.s0.tips: The antiques market runs on Saturdays (other days only the shops are open). Look out for the pastel houses of Notting Hill.
strings.d4.s1.name: Kensington Palace Gardens
strings.d4.s1.tips: The gardens of Kensington Palace and the Princess Diana memorial. Entry to the palace itself is ~24 GBP.
strings.d4.s2.name: The Churchill Arms
strings.d4.s2.tips: A pub covered in flowers, with Thai food inside. A London classic.
strings.d4.s3.name: Natural History Museum
strings.d4.s3.tips: Dinosaur skeletons and a blue whale. Free entry; head for Hintze Hall.
strings.d4.s4.name: Hyde Park & Serpentine
strings.d4.s4.tips: The Serpentine lake and Speakers' Corner. Rent a boat in summer.
strings.d4.b0.name: Victoria and Albert Museum
strings.d4.b0.tips: A design museum. Free entry, with a café in the courtyard.
strings.d4.b1.name: Ottolenghi Notting Hill
strings.d4.b1.tips: A display of salads and pastries.
strings.d5.s0.name: Camden Market
strings.d5.s0.tips: 1,000 stalls selling street food and punk-vintage clothes, including Stables Market.
strings.d5.s1.name: Camden Lock Street Food
strings.d5.s1.tips: The market's food court, with cuisines from around the world.
strings.d5.s2.name: Regent's Canal Walk
strings.d5.s2.tips: Follow the canal from Camden to Little Venice, past narrowboats.
strings.d5.s3.name: Primrose Hill
strings.d5.s3.tips: The best free view of the London skyline.
strings.d5.s4.name: Regent's Park Rose Garden
strings.d5.s4.tips: Queen Mary's Gardens, with 12,000 roses in summer.
strings.d5.b0.name: The Engineer Primrose Hill
strings.d5.b1.name: ZSL London Zoo
strings.d5.b1.tips: A zoo in Regent's Park, good if you're travelling with children.
strings.d6.s0.name: Uber Boat Thames Clipper
strings.d6.s0.tips: The river bus from Westminster to Greenwich (Oyster accepted). You pass under the bridges.
strings.d6.s1.name: Cutty Sark
strings.d6.s1.tips: A tea clipper. Walk along the deck.
strings.d6.s2.name: Greenwich Market
strings.d6.s2.tips: A weekend market of handicrafts and street food.
strings.d6.s3.name: Royal Observatory Greenwich
strings.d6.s3.tips: The Prime Meridian line and a planetarium. There are views from the top of the park.
strings.d6.s4.name: Greenwich Park
strings.d6.s4.tips: From the hill you can see Canary Wharf and the river. Good for a picnic.
strings.d6.b0.name: Goddards at Greenwich
strings.d6.b1.name: National Maritime Museum
strings.d6.b1.tips: A free maritime museum, an alternative to the observatory.
strings.d7.theme: Sunday roast and a gentle farewell
strings.d7.s0.name: Columbia Road Flower Market
strings.d7.s0.tips: A flower market on Sundays (on other days, street cafés only). In the East End.
strings.d7.s1.name: Brick Lane
strings.d7.s1.tips: Street art, vintage shops and bagels (Beigel Bake is open 24 hours).
strings.d7.s2.name: The Cat and Mutton Broadway Market
strings.d7.s2.tips: One of London's best Sunday roasts. Reserve for Sunday; on other days there's a pub menu.
strings.d7.s3.name: Liverpool Street Station
strings.d7.s3.tips: Heathrow is 45 minutes away on the Elizabeth Line. Time to say goodbye.
strings.d7.b0.name: Beigel Bake Brick Lane
strings.d7.b0.tips: Salt beef bagel, a quick farewell bite.
strings.d7.b1.name: Spitalfields Market
strings.d7.b1.tips: An indoor market, an alternative to Brick Lane.
strings.note0: Pay with a contactless card or Oyster for a daily cap (~9 GBP). Buses are cheaper than the Tube and the upper deck has views. Take the Elizabeth Line to Heathrow.
strings.note1: The big museums are free (British Museum, Tate, Natural History Museum, V&A). The Tower, Westminster Abbey and St Paul's charge entry, and online tickets are cheaper.
strings.note2: Summer temperatures are 20-25°C, but rain is possible. Enjoy parks and river trips in summer, with daylight lasting until 21:30.
strings.note3: Pub culture: order at the bar and don't tip. Restaurants may add a 12.5% service charge.
strings.note4: Borough Market is closed on Mondays; Portobello is a Saturday market and Columbia Road a Sunday one.
strings.note5: Reserve for Sunday roast. Pie and mash, fish and chips and Dishoom are London classics.
strings.transit.name: Oyster / Contactless
strings.transit.why_chosen: The cheapest option thanks to the daily cap on the Tube, buses, DLR and trains. A contactless card does the same job.
